paragraphs.title: The Drought and the Suffering in the Land

easy.explanation: The passage concerns a severe drought, or dearth.
easy.q: What is the main subject of these verses?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “Judah mourneth, and the gates thereof languish.”
easy.q: What happened to the gates of Judah?

easy.explanation: They came to the pits but found no water.
easy.q: What did the nobles’ messengers fail to find?

medium.explanation: The ground was cracked because there had been no rain.
medium.q: Why were the plowmen ashamed and covering their heads?

answers: The hind forsook her calf and the wild asses found no grass
medium.explanation: The animals suffered because there was no grass.
medium.q: How did the drought affect the animals?

medium.explanation: Covering the head represents shame and sorrow.
medium.q: What does “covered their heads” express in this context?

answers: The city, the farmers, the messengers, and the animals
The land, the city, the messengers, and the animals
The gates, the messengers, the farmers, and the animals
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from the land to the city, water-seekers, and animals.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the spread of the suffering?

challenge.explanation: Both farmers and messengers were ashamed because their needs could not be met.
challenge.q: What does the repeated description of shame show?

answers: Even the wild animals found no grass
challenge.explanation: The drought harmed animals as well as people.
challenge.q: Which detail especially emphasizes the severity of the drought?

paragraphs.title: The People’s Prayer and Their Sense of God’s Absence

easy.explanation: They say, “we have sinned against thee.”

answers: The hope of Israel and its saviour
easy.explanation: The Lord is called “the hope of Israel” and “the saviour thereof.”
easy.q: What titles are given to the Lord in the prayer?

answers: That the farmers not be punished
That the Lord not leave them
easy.q: What does the people ask at the end of the prayer?

answers: They deny their sins and then pray
They confess their sins yet still ask for help
They ask for help without mentioning sin
medium.explanation: They acknowledge their backslidings while appealing to the Lord as Savior.
medium.q: How does the people combine confession with prayer?

answers: They feel that He is distant from them
The Lord has just arrived in the land
They want to leave the land
medium.explanation: The comparison expresses a sense that the Lord is not helping them.
medium.q: Why does the people ask whether the Lord will be “as a stranger in the land”?

medium.explanation: The Lord is presented as the one in whom Israel hopes.
medium.q: What does “the hope of Israel” mean in this passage?

challenge.explanation: The people confess sin while continuing to hope in the Lord.
challenge.q: What central tension appears in the people’s prayer?

answers: The relationship and belonging between the Lord and His people
That the people do not know the Lord
That the people want a human king
challenge.explanation: The phrase appeals to the people’s connection with the Lord.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “we are called by thy name” emphasize?

answers: They see Him as their source of help in trouble
He is one of Judah’s farmers
He searched the pits for water
challenge.explanation: Their distress leads them to appeal to the Lord as their deliverer.
challenge.q: Why is it important that the people call the Lord their saviour during the drought?

paragraphs.title: The Rejection of the People and the Judgment

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “Thus have they loved to wander.”
easy.q: What did the people love to do?

answers: Do not pray for their good
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “Pray not for this people for their good.”
easy.q: What did the Lord command concerning prayer for the people?

easy.explanation: The Lord names the sword, famine, and pestilence.
easy.q: By what three means would judgment come?

answers: They loved to wander in their own ways, so the Lord would not accept them
They kept every commandment, so they were tested
They did not know how to pray
medium.explanation: Their persistent wandering is given as the reason for rejection.
medium.q: What connection does the Lord make between the people’s conduct and the rejection of their prayers?

answers: Fasting, crying, burnt offerings, and oblations
medium.explanation: The Lord would not hear their cry or accept their offerings.
medium.q: Which religious acts would not be accepted?

medium.explanation: The word describes the people’s repeated turning away from the Lord.

answers: Religious acts are not enough without a change in conduct
The people did not understand fasting
challenge.explanation: The passage links rejected worship with the people’s sinful behavior.
challenge.q: What does the rejection of fasting, prayer, and offerings teach?

answers: It identifies the people’s sin, rejects their appeals, and then announces punishment
It begins with deliverance and ends with sin
challenge.explanation: The order connects sin, rejected worship, and judgment.
challenge.q: How does the passage build a sense of certainty about judgment?

answers: He will call their sins to account and punish them
He will immediately erase their sins
The people will forget their sins
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes divine judgment for their wrongdoing.
challenge.q: What does it mean that the Lord will “remember their iniquity, and visit their sins”?

paragraphs.title: The False Prophets and Their Punishment

easy.explanation: They said there would be no sword or famine and promised assured peace.
easy.q: What did the other prophets promise?

easy.explanation: The Lord calls their message a false vision and divination.
easy.q: How does the Lord describe their messages?

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “I sent them not.”
easy.q: Who did not send these prophets?

answers: The Lord had not sent, commanded, or spoken to them
medium.explanation: The Lord explicitly denies sending or speaking to them.
medium.q: Why were the other prophets false?

answers: They would be consumed by sword and famine
medium.explanation: The Lord says, “By sword and famine shall those prophets be consumed.”
medium.q: What would happen to the false prophets?

answers: Thrown or left in the streets
medium.explanation: The people would be left lying in Jerusalem’s streets.
medium.q: What does “cast out in the streets” mean?

answers: The false promise led people to trust a lie, so both prophets and hearers would suffer
The promise of peace prevented judgment
challenge.explanation: The judgment includes both the false prophets and the people who followed them.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the promise of peace and the punishment?

answers: They prophesied in the Lord’s name even though He had not sent them
challenge.explanation: They spoke in the Lord’s name, but He denied commissioning them.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the prophets wrongly claimed divine authority?

answers: To show the widespread extent of the disaster
To show that the famine had ended
challenge.explanation: The list emphasizes that the calamity affected the whole community.
challenge.q: Why does the punishment mention wives, sons, and daughters?

easy.explanation: He was told to declare a message of grief over the great breach.
easy.q: What was Jeremiah told to speak to the people?

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “Let mine eyes run down with tears night and day.”
easy.q: When were Jeremiah’s tears to flow?

easy.explanation: He saw people slain with the sword.
easy.q: What did Jeremiah see in the field?

medium.explanation: In the city he saw those suffering from famine.
medium.q: What did Jeremiah see in the city?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes the people’s severe destruction and suffering.
medium.q: What does “a great breach” mean here?

answers: They go about in a land they do not know
They lead the people to victory
medium.explanation: Both are wandering in an unfamiliar land.
medium.q: How are the prophet and priest described?

answers: The field and the city suffer different forms of disaster
Only the rich and poor are contrasted
challenge.explanation: The field has victims of the sword, while the city has victims of famine.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in Jeremiah’s description?

answers: He deeply identifies with the people’s suffering
He is indifferent to the disaster
He promises that everything will end immediately
challenge.explanation: His unceasing tears show profound grief.
challenge.q: What does Jeremiah’s continual weeping reveal about him?

answers: Even the prophet and priest wander without knowing where they are
There is no famine in the city
challenge.explanation: The confusion and suffering reach religious leaders as well.
challenge.q: Which easily overlooked detail helps explain the scope of the disaster?

paragraphs.title: Confession and a Plea to Renew the Covenant

answers: Their wickedness and their fathers’ iniquity
easy.explanation: They acknowledge their wickedness and the iniquity of their fathers.
They plead, “break not thy covenant with us.”
easy.q: What does the people ask concerning the covenant?

easy.explanation: The prayer declares that the Lord alone can give rain.
easy.q: Who does the people say can cause rain?

medium.explanation: The people ask the Lord not to despise or reject them.
medium.q: What does the request “Do not abhor us, for thy name’s sake” mean?

answers: The people confess their sins yet ask that their relationship with the Lord not be cut off
They deny their sins and ask for wealth
They ask to replace the covenant
medium.explanation: Their confession is followed by a plea for continued covenant relationship.
medium.q: How is confession connected with the plea concerning the covenant?

answers: The people admit their sins yet still hope for the Lord’s mercy
The people reject the Lord and do not pray
The people say rain is unnecessary
challenge.explanation: Their confession is joined with a plea not to be abandoned.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast at the end of the chapter?

answers: It presents Him as the maker of all things and the giver of rain
It credits the Gentiles’ vanities with rain
It says no one can give rain
challenge.explanation: The people reject false powers and wait upon the Lord.
challenge.q: How does the final verse support the claim that the Lord is the source of hope?

answers: The people ask that the Lord’s honor and relationship with them not be disgraced
They ask for a new chair
challenge.explanation: The request connects the Lord’s glory with the preservation of His covenant.
challenge.q: Why is “the throne of thy glory” mentioned beside the request not to break the covenant?
